questions: Daniel kept a daily time with God for decades while living in a culture that didn't follow God. What makes a daily rhythm with God hard in our house right now?
Daniel 9:18 says Daniel came to God "based on your abundant compassion," not his own good record. How does that change the way we think about the days we miss?
prayForStudents: Pray students build a daily rhythm with God and remember His grace on the days they miss.

guide.summary: This week's message, Rhythms, wrapped up our Prayer and Worship series. Students looked at three rhythms that keep faith growing. From Daniel 9, they saw a man who read God's Word and then prayed it back to God. From Acts 2:42-47, they saw the early church devoted to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer together. From Acts 9 and 1 Timothy 1, they saw how God's mercy met Saul, a man far from Him. The big idea: Grace starts it. Rhythm keeps it. Students were challenged to try the Daniel Window: same time, same place, Bible before apps, read one short passage, and pray one honest line back to God.
guide.keyVerse: "For we are not presenting our petitions before you based on our righteous acts, but based on your abundant compassion." Daniel 9:18 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: Daniel kept a daily time with God for decades while living in a culture that didn't follow God. What makes a daily rhythm with God hard in our house right now?
Daniel came to God based on God's compassion, not his own good record. How does that change the way we think about the days we miss?
The early church in Acts 2 grew in faith together. What is one way our family could make time with God something we do together?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Try the Daniel Window as a family: pick a set time and place, Bible before phones, read one short passage together, and each pray one honest sentence back to God. If you miss a day, just start again. Grace starts it. Rhythm keeps it.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that we come to You because of Your compassion and not because we have it all together. Help our family build a rhythm of time with You. When we miss a day, remind us that Your grace is still there, and help us start again. Amen.

questions: When worry starts piling up, what helps you feel steadier, and how can I help?
prayForStudents: Pray students who feel anxious know God cares, and find steadiness through prayer and gratitude.

questions: If a friend felt really down for a long time, what do you think would help them most?
prayForStudents: Pray students facing heavy days know they are not alone and can bring despair to God with hope.

questions: What helps you feel secure in who you are, even when friendships feel shaky?
prayForStudents: Pray students find secure love in Christ and build healthy relationships from that security.
